What is a
Credit Score?

A credit score is a 3-digit numerical value depicting your creditworthiness; your ability to manage and repay debt. The value calculated by Experian Credit Information Company of India Private Limited ranges between 300 and 900. It considers your credit report, which includes factors such as credit utilization, types of credit used, payment history, length of credit history, and recent credit inquiries.

Lenders assess the score to understand the risk associated with sanctioning a loan to you. The higher your credit score, the lower the risk, the better the interest rates and loan terms. Maintaining a score over 750 boosts your financial health and positively influences loan approvals.
What is the Importance
of a CIBIL Score?

The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited (CIBIL) calculates and issues your CIBIL score, and it ranges from 300 to 900. Financial institutions like banks and NBFCs refer to this score when assessing loan or credit card applications.

A higher score signifies a stronger credit profile and increases the chances of quicker approvals, better interest rates, and higher loan amounts. Conversely, a low score may lead to application rejections or borrowing at unfavorable terms.

What is a Good
Credit Score?

A credit score above 700 is considered good, and above 760 is considered excellent. Maintaining a good credit score helps you easily secure loans or credit cards with favorable terms. You must pay your debts on time and manage your credit products, such as personal or home loans, responsibly to build and maintain a good credit score.
How a Credit Score
is Calculated?
Credit bureaus, licensed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), calculate an individual’s credit score after considering the following factors:
Credit Utilisation
The sanctioned debt amount contributes 30% to your score. Spending more than your salary or exhausting a credit card’s monthly limit can negatively impact your credit score.
Credit Type and Repayment Duration
The type of loan you apply for affects 10% of your score. By applying for secured and non-secured loans, you can maintain a credit balance. Likewise, repayment contributes 15% to your score.
Credit Enquiries

Each time you apply for a loan, it reflects on your credit report. So taking multiple loans in short intervals can hurt your credit profile. Similarly, each rejection also reflects on your credit report. Hence, it is advised to apply for a loan only when you are sure of being able to repay it in a timely manner.
Benefits of a Good
Credit Score
A good credit score improves loan eligibility, and loan approval chances and increases your likelihood of landing competitive loan terms. Check your online credit score for free with Tata Capital.
The various benefits of a credit score above 750 are:
Higher Chances of Approval

A high credit score reflects your creditworthiness and clean credit history to potential lenders. This credit score means lenders trust your ability to repay the loan amount. High online credit score results in quick approval, faster loan processing, and a speedy fund disbursal.
Better Interest Rates

High credit score benefits also include being able to negotiate better terms. A high online credit score can help you qualify for attractive loan interest rates, reducing your overall repayment amount.
Higher Loan Amount
Since a good credit score indicates dependable credit behaviour, you can bag a bigger loan amount at competitive interest rates.
Pre-approved Loan Offer

If you have a sound financial background, high credit score, and a disciplined credit report free of loan defaults, lenders can also pitch your pre-approved loan offers. Besides, since the lending institution performs a credit score check online and pre-approves you a loan amount, your online credit score will land attractive interest rates and flexible loan tenures.
Why Your Credit Score Matters
for Loan Approval
When you apply for a loan or credit card, lenders don't just look at your income. They also perform a CIBIL score check.

A strong score signals responsible credit behavior, making lenders more confident in your ability to repay. It directly influences your interest rate, loan amount, and approval speed. A low score, on the other hand, can lead to rejections or unfavorable terms.
This is why it helps to know how to check your credit score online and stay on top of any changes before making a major credit application.
How to
Improve Your Credit Score?

If you don’t have a good credit score, you can bring your credit score up in a matter of months with disciplined credit and repayment behaviour. Check your online credit score and maintain a healthy credit score through-
Consistently pay your loan Equated Monthly Instalments (EMIs) and credit card bills on time. A credit report free of EMI defaults and late payments perks up your credit score.
Regularly check your online credit score for any discrepancies and understand your potential loan eligibility.
Your online credit score should have a healthy mix of unsecured and secured credit. Here, the fewer unsecured loans you have active, the better your credit score.
Your credit utilisation on your credit card must be 30%-35% or lower than your current credit limit. However, not using your card at all can also lower your credit score.
Before applying for a new loan, check your credit history online. Credit score can reduce if you service multiple loans simultaneously and apply for new credit as well.
Common Mistakes
That Lower Credit Score
If you want to learn how to improve your credit score quickly, make sure to avoid these mistakes and protect your borrowing power:
Late or missed payments have the most significant impact on your score. Timely payments are non-negotiable.
Payment history:
Using more than 30% of your available credit is a common misstep. Keeping utilization low is the key to maintaining a good CIBIL score.
Credit utilization:
Closing old accounts shortens your credit history, which can hurt your score. Older accounts signal stability to lenders.
Credit history:

Applying for multiple loans or cards in a short period triggers several hard inquiries, which can drag your score down. Do a free credit score check without affecting your score to monitor your standing without adding inquiries.
Multiple credit inquiries:
Relying too heavily on one type of credit, like only credit cards, limits your profile. A diverse mix of loans and cards reflects responsible credit management.
Credit mix:
Most of these mistakes are reversible. Regularly doing a CIBIL score check helps you catch issues early and course-correct before they affect your next loan or card application.
How Often Should You
Check Credit Score?

Checking your score regularly is a healthy financial habit and does not hurt your score. You should check your credit score at least once every three to four months, or before applying for any loan or credit card.

If you've recently missed a payment or closed an account, check sooner. You can learn how to check your credit score online at any time through bureau websites or lender platforms. Staying informed helps you spot errors, track progress, and avoid surprises during loan applications.
Is Checking
Credit Score Safe?
Performing an instant credit score check is completely safe and very convenient nowadays.

When you check your credit score in India, it counts as a soft inquiry and has no impact on your score whatsoever. You can do a free credit score check without affecting your score as many times as you need. Only hard inquiries, which are triggered when a lender pulls your score after a loan application, can temporarily affect your score. So, there's no reason to hold back.
The more regularly you perform free credit score checks, the better positioned you are to catch discrepancies and maintain a healthy credit profile.

Credit Bureaus
in India

A credit bureau is an agency creating credit scores by collecting and analysing credit data, including credit cards used, loans taken, overdraft facilities, etc., associated with people or business entities.
TransUnion CIBIL Limited

CIBIL is India’s first Credit Information Company (CIC). CIBIL bureau collates and maintains records of every individual’s repayment habits and credit behaviour for loans and credit cards. It then creates credit scores and Credit Information Reports (CIR). The CIBIL report and online Credit score help lenders make lending decisions.
Experian Credit Information Company of India Private Limited

Experian is a Dublin-based credit bureau using different methods to create a credit report. This credit score check online reveals an individual’s loan and credit history collated from India’s member banks and other financial establishments.
Equifax Credit Information Services Private Limited (ECIS)

One of the oldest credit bureaus in the US, Equifax offers credit scores and reports for individuals and businesses. It ties up with India’s financial institutions to create credit scores and credit reports.
CRIF High Mark

This credit bureau specialises in scoring, analytics, and credit management solutions. It makes credit reports with information from banks, NBFCs, Income Tax Department, etc. The online Credit score report from CRIF High Mark is available at a fee.

How Long Does It Take to
Improve a Credit Score?

There's no fixed timeline, but consistent habits can show meaningful results within three to six months. More significant improvements, especially after defaults or high debt periods, can take six to twelve months of disciplined behavior.
If you're wondering how to improve your credit score quickly, start with the basics: clear any overdue payments, bring credit utilization below 30%, and avoid applying for new credit unnecessarily.
Do a free credit score check periodically to track your progress and adjust your habits based on what's affecting your score most.

FAQs
How and where are credit scores used?
Your credit score is calculated based on your credit history, repayment records, and other credit information in your credit report.

So before approving a loan, lenders use your score to measure your creditworthiness as a borrower. Telecom companies use your report and score to verify your details and gauge your ability to pay post-paid bills timely.
Why is PAN card required for checking credit score?

Your PAN is unique and linked to all your financial transactions. Credit bureaus use your PAN as a unique identifier to locate your credit information in their records. This is why you need to provide your PAN to check your credit score online.
Enter your PAN and get your free credit score check online with Tata Capital.
Can credit score inquiries affect the score?
Yes, some types of inquiries can affect your score.
When you apply for a credit card or a loan, lenders perform a credit check, which reflects in your credit report as a hard inquiry. Hard inquiries can decrease your credit score.
However, employer credit checks and self credit checks are soft inquiries and do not affect your score.
What are the important factors to maintain a good credit score?
Tips for a good credit score:
Avoid having too many loans and active credit cards simultaneously.
Pay your credit card bills timely.
Keep your credit utilisation under 30% of your credit limit.
Be consistent and punctual with your EMI repayments.
Check your credit score online and report regularly, and notify credit bureaus about any mistakes.
What is the difference between Credit Score provided by Experian Credit Information Company of India Private Limited & Credit Score provided by TransUnion CIBIL Limited?
The credit score is set by the Reserve bank of India (RBI), ranging from 300 to 900, with 900 being the highest. There are various credit bureaus, Experian and CIBIL TransUnion being among them.

Experian and CIBIL TransUnion are well-known credit information companies approved by the Securities and Exchange Board (SEBI). They provide detailed credit reports that aid various lenders and borrowers in making informed decisions. A credit score of 750 and above is considered suitable for CIBIL and Experian.
Some points of distinction:

CIBIL caters primarily to domestic money lenders; hence, preferred by most financial institutions in India. International financial institutions like HSBC and Morgan Stanley favour Experian score. Being an Indian-based establishment, Credit scores are given more priority by Indian lenders.

CIBIL and Experian provide the status and detailed credit reports of a company and individual. However, since 90% of the companies and financial institutions are linked with CIBIL, you have a better chance of getting your loan approved with a positive Credit score.

Both use different algorithms to compute the credit score. For instance, CIBIL uses the algorithm Empirica, which collects data on payment history, credit type, credit utilisation, and credit exposures. In contrast, Experian uses the FIFO (First In, First Out) to calculate the credit score.
Who computes the Credit Score?

Credit scores are computed by credit bureaus in India. These include Equifax, CRIF High Mark, CIBIL TransUnion and Experian. Financial institutions and lenders rely on the scores attributed by these credit bureaus to ascertain a borrower’s creditworthiness.
Why should I check my Credit Score?

You should check your credit score online to ascertain your current credit position. Since financial institutions and lenders rely on your credit score to determine your creditworthiness, ensuring your credit score is error-free and accurately reflects your creditworthiness is crucial to a successful loan application.
Is credit score of 750 considered good?
Yes, a credit score of 750 is generally considered good. It reflects strong creditworthiness, increasing your chances of loan approvals and favourable terms from lenders.
Can anyone check my credit score?
No, only authorized entities, such as lenders, financial institutions, or you yourself, can check the credit score. Unauthorized individuals cannot access your credit score without your consent.
What is the minimum credit score to get any loan?
The minimum credit score to secure a loan varies with financial institutions. Be sure to discuss this with your chosen lender.
Why does my credit score keep changing?
Your credit score changes due to factors like payment history, credit utilization, new credit inquiries, account age, and credit mix.
How is my credit score determined?
Your credit score is calculated based on payment history, credit usage, etc.

Why do lenders check your CIBIL score before approving your loan?

Lenders check your CIBIL score before approving a loan to assess your creditworthiness and repayment history. A high score indicates responsible credit behavior, reducing the risk of default. It helps lenders decide loan approval, set interest rates, and determine your loan eligibility.
Who calculates credit scores?
Credit bureaus like CIBIL, Experian, Equifax, and CRIF High Mark calculate credit scores. They analyze your credit history, repayment behavior, and financial activity to generate your credit score.
How often is my credit score updated?

Credit bureaus typically update your score once a month, after receiving the latest repayment and account data from your lenders and financial institutions. You must check your score with your PAN and phone number periodically to keep track of how your score changes with each update.
How long does negative information stay on a credit report?
Most negative information, including missed payments and defaults, stays on your credit report for up to seven years, depending on the bureau's reporting guidelines.
How can I improve my credit score quickly?
Pay all dues on time, reduce credit card utilization, avoid multiple loan applications, and regularly check your credit score to track improvements and catch errors early.
Which loans affect credit score the most?
Unsecured loans like personal loans and credit cards have the most impact. Multiple active unsecured loans or frequent defaults on these can significantly lower your score.
What information is included in a credit report?
A credit report includes your personal details, account history, repayment behavior, credit inquiries, and any defaults or settlements recorded by lenders and financial institutions.
